questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took 6 courses, which was a lot—48 ECTS in total. This included 3 undergraduate courses and 3 graduate courses.

Fluid Dynamics: The teaching was mediocre, but there was a textbook available for self-study. The tests were poorly designed, and the workload was massive.

Hypersonic Vehicle Design: Honestly, this didn’t feel like a real course. The professor would talk for 1.5 hours straight about PowerPoint slides with pictures of "hypersonic vehicles," but there was no homework or any other material to learn from. There was one midterm, but we never got the results—I suspect everyone did so poorly that the professor just ignored it. For the final, I drew what I thought looked like a fast vehicle, talked about it for five minutes, and got the equivalent of a 10 for that. I learned literally nothing.

Ocean Wave Propagation Theory: This was by far the best course. I actually learned something, likely because there were only three students in the class, and I was the only English-speaking one in this "English" course. As a result, the professor tailored the education to me.

Power System Economics: I don’t think the professor even knew what he wanted to teach in this course. He had a midlife crisis during the semester, declaring he wouldn’t be teaching in this field anymore because “nothing in life matters” and “the whole industry is a scam.”

Numerical Analysis: This was actually a challenging course, especially since the teaching style was just 1.5 hours of continuous lecturing. I ended up relying heavily on the textbook connected to the course, which helped me scrape through the tests. Keep in mind that the average test score here was around 25–30%, meaning you could theoretically score 30% on all tests and still get an A+. It felt like there was no system at all—professors just did whatever they wanted.

Atomic Physics: This was the only real physics course I could choose, so I was pretty excited about it. Unfortunately, I didn’t really learn anything. One-third of the lectures were pre-recorded MP4 files, one-third were in-person, and the remaining third didn’t happen because the professor’s iPad broke, and he couldn’t record the videos. He scheduled the exam at the same time as one of my other exams, so he arranged a special oral exam just for me. His teaching consisted of writing down everything he said on the blackboard for 1.5 hours without including any formulas or calculations throughout the course.

questions.answer:
Explore seoul it is a huge place.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: SNU buddy program, kinda random how good koreans are at english.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Koreans are kinda rude on the outside, no one holds the door for you, no one really says good morning, it kinda feels like you don't exist. But they are nice when you get to know them, although very insecure in my opinion. I think Korea has a lot of problems with beauty standards and being over worked.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The eating out culture, being able to just meet with your friends, having fun and then going to resturants without running your pocket empty was nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't care about education as you aren't going to learn much. (Atleast in the case of Physics and Engineering)
If you show up and hand in homework you will most likely pass.
Join SNU buddy program.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot, but tbh, just get a korean buddy from the buddy program and ask them if you run into any struggles.
A lot of stuff will not make sence, and that is just how it is, there is no reason for it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to learn something.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Sign up for the ARC creation/meetup date before you go to Korea. They might tell you that you can only schedule an appointment after you arrive in Korea, but this is not true. Just book an appointment and go as soon as you arrive. The group application process through SNU takes about two months, and you really need the ARC to handle many essential things. Some of my friends only received theirs two days before leaving.
